channel.title: BudgetGo Blog
channel.description: Practical guides on budgeting, tracking spending, and getting the most out of BudgetGo.

item.title: Zero-Based Budgeting, Explained (With a Monthly Example)
item.description: Zero-based budgeting explained step by step: how to give every dollar of take-home pay a job, a full $4,200 monthly example, how to handle irregular income, and how to run it in BudgetGo.

item.title: 7 Ways to Get Your Spending Into BudgetGo (and Which Ones to Use)
item.description: Voice, Apple Pay, bank SMS alerts, Apple Wallet, connected banks, statement imports and manual entry: every way to add spending to BudgetGo, and the best setup for you.

item.title: Voice Expense Tracking: Log Spending by Just Saying It
item.description: Voice expense tracking lets you log a purchase by saying it out loud. Here's how it works, what to say, when it beats automatic tracking, and how to make it a 10-second habit.

item.title: Turn Bank SMS Alerts Into a Spending Tracker (Apple Shortcuts Guide)
item.description: How to track spending from bank SMS alerts automatically: set up an Apple Shortcuts Message automation, keep it limited to your bank, and fix it when an alert doesn't log.

item.title: Spending by Merchant: Why Your Top Merchants Say More Than Your Categories
item.description: How to track spending by merchant to see where your money really goes: a worked monthly example, the five kinds of merchants to look for, the visit-times-average math, and how to act on what you find.

item.title: Safe to Spend: How BudgetGo Forecasts the Rest of Your Month
item.description: What "safe to spend" means, how a spending forecast works (with the math), and how BudgetGo's Forecast and Safe to Spend help you stay on track for the rest of the month.

item.title: How to Stop Impulse Spending Without Feeling Deprived (With the Math)
item.description: How to stop impulse spending without cutting out every treat: find your triggers, add a pause before you buy, give yourself a planned fun-money cap, and track it so the holiday sales don't take over.

item.title: How to Import a Bank Statement (PDF, CSV or Excel) Into a Budget App
item.description: How to import a bank statement into a budget app step by step: download the right file from your bank, choose PDF, CSV or Excel, avoid duplicates, and check the results.

item.title: How to Stop Overspending Every Month (With the Math)
item.description: How to stop overspending without guessing: measure your monthly gap, find the two categories causing it, set a weekly cap, and keep credit cards from hiding the overspend until the bill arrives.

item.title: How to Save Money on Your Heating Bill This Winter (With the Math)
item.description: How to save money on your heating bill this winter: estimate your monthly heating cost, make the cheap fixes that matter, and plan the winter months in your budget so a cold snap doesn't wreck it.

item.title: How to Save Money for Christmas in 6 Weeks (With the Math)
item.description: How to save money for Christmas with about six weeks to go: set a target, split it across your remaining paychecks, find the cash in your own spending, and start next year's Christmas fund in January.

item.title: How to Make a Budget From Scratch in 5 Steps (With the Math)
item.description: How to make a budget from scratch in 5 steps: find your take-home pay, list what you really spend, do the math, set savings targets, and adjust after month one. Includes a full $3,800 example.

item.title: How to Avoid Holiday Debt This Year (With a Worked Example)
item.description: How to avoid holiday debt in 2026: find the cash you'll actually have by December 31, close the gap before you shop, use buy now, pay later safely, and track every purchase so January starts clean.

item.title: How Much Should You Spend on Groceries? (With the Math)
item.description: How much to spend on groceries per month, worked out from your own numbers: track three months, set a weekly cap, split it into a weekly shop and a stock-up, and watch your pace so food costs stop drifting.

item.title: How Much Should You Spend on Eating Out? (With the Math)
item.description: How much to spend on eating out per month, worked out from your own numbers: check what you spend now, compare it with US averages, set a monthly number and a per-meal limit, and track it so it stops creeping up.

item.title: Insight Stories: How BudgetGo Turns Your Spending Into a One-Minute Recap
item.description: BudgetGo turns your transactions into short, tappable insight stories: pacing, saving opportunities, overspending, hidden habits and period comparisons. Here's how they work.

item.title: How BudgetGo's AI Categorizes Your Transactions (and Keeps You in Control)
item.description: How BudgetGo uses AI to categorize every transaction automatically, from bank feeds, Apple Pay, SMS alerts and statements, and how you can review or change any category.

item.title: Holiday Tipping Guide: Who to Tip and How Much (With the Math)
item.description: A holiday tipping guide that starts with your budget: who to tip, how much to give your mail carrier, cleaner, teacher and others, and a worked example that adds it all up.

item.title: How to Make a Holiday Budget (With a Worked Example)
item.description: How to make a holiday budget in 6 steps: list every cost, set a total you can pay without debt, split it by category, and track it. Includes a worked example with the math.

item.title: The 5-Minute End-of-Month Budget Review (Step by Step)
item.description: A 5-minute end-of-month budget review: close out the month, check one number, find the categories that drifted, work out why, and make one change for next month. With a worked example.

item.title: Cash Flow, Explained: Money In vs Money Out (With an Example)
item.description: Personal cash flow explained simply: the money in minus money out formula, a worked monthly example, what positive and negative cash flow mean, the counting mistakes to avoid, and how to improve yours.

item.title: Are Budgeting Apps Safe? How BudgetGo Uses AI Without Selling Your Data
item.description: Are budgeting apps safe to use with AI? What happens to your spending data in BudgetGo: what the AI sees, who processes it, what we never do with it, and the privacy controls you keep.

item.title: Should You Set a Budget or Just Track Your Spending?
item.description: Should you set a budget or just track your spending? The difference between budgeting and expense tracking, when tracking alone is enough, when you need a budget, and how to move from one to the other.

item.title: How to Do a No-Spend Challenge (and Make It Stick)
item.description: How to do a no-spend challenge that lasts: set the rules, decide what counts as essential, work out what you'll save with real math, track every day, and plan the day after.

item.title: How to Track Apple Pay Spending Automatically (Step by Step)
item.description: How to track Apple Pay spending automatically with an Apple Shortcuts automation: set it up in about two minutes, see what gets captured, and fix it when a payment doesn't show up.

item.title: How Much Does Thanksgiving Dinner Cost? (Budget Per Person, With the Math)
item.description: How much Thanksgiving dinner costs in 2026, and how to set your own budget per person: a worked example for 10 guests, ways to trim the bill, and how to track it before Thursday, November 26.

item.title: How BudgetGo Finds Your Subscriptions and Bills Before They Hit
item.description: How to track subscriptions and recurring bills automatically: how BudgetGo spots repeating charges, lines up what's due this week, and helps you plan before the money leaves.

item.title: How Much Should You Spend on Black Friday? (With a Budget Example)
item.description: How much to spend on Black Friday, worked out from your own numbers: set a ceiling, build a ranked list, cap impulse buys, and track every deal so the sales don't wreck your December.

item.title: How Much Should You Spend on Christmas Gifts? (With the Math)
item.description: How much to spend on Christmas gifts, worked out from your own numbers: set a total you can afford, split it per person and per child, and track it so December doesn't spill into January.

item.title: How to Track Your Spending Without a Spreadsheet
item.description: A simple 4-step system to track your spending automatically, sort it into categories, and spot where your money goes, no spreadsheet needed.

item.title: How to Find and Cancel Subscriptions You Forgot About
item.description: A quick subscription audit: how to find every recurring charge, check App Store subscriptions, decide what to cancel, and stop surprise renewals.

item.title: The 50/30/20 Budget Rule, Explained With a Real Example
item.description: What the 50/30/20 budget rule is, how to split your take-home pay into needs, wants, and savings, and how to adjust it when rent is high.
